description: We are a team of third-year Electrical and Electronics Engineering students. Our team has 2 coders and 2 Figma designers. We are building an interactive story about NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars, so school-age students can learn about the rovers, landers and probes and the science they made possible. Our team is complete.
summary: Echoes of Silence is an interactive, gamified storytelling web application designed to introduce school-age and casual space enthusiasts to NASA’s discarded and still-traveling space hardware across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Blending emotional first-person narratives with authentic NASA mission telemetry, the app transforms historic rovers, landers, and probes into living storytellers—allowing users to explore their resting places, play interactive mini-missions, and discover the groundbreaking scientific breakthroughs each machine made possible.
details: What It Does: Echoes of Silence: The Artifact Odyssey is an interactive, gamified educational web application built for the "Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" challenge. Users explore a calm, cosmic interface featuring celestial hubs (The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space) to locate iconic NASA hardware left behind after historic missions—including the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Mars Opportunity Rover, InSight Lander, Cassini Orbiter, and Voyager 1. ​How It Works & Key Features: ​First-Person Emotional Storytelling: Each artifact speaks directly to young learners in a poetic, accessible voice, chronicling its launch, discoveries, and final moments. ​Hardware-to-Science Connection: Every story pairs narrative storytelling with verified NASA scientific achievements—from lunar laser retroreflectors and Martian hematite "blueberries" to marsquake seismology, Enceladus's ice geysers, and Voyager's Golden Record. ​Gamified Mini-Interactions: Each artifact features a unique interactive mechanic—such as clearing Martian dust from Opportunity’s solar panels, tuning InSight’s seismic wave dial, bouncing a laser off Apollo 11's retroreflector, and playing Voyager’s Golden Record. ​Tools, Languages & Hardware Used: Built using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5/CSS3, GitHub for version control, and deployed live on Vercel. Generative AI tools (Google AI Studio / Gemini) were used to assist in rapid code scaffolding and narrative structuring. ​Intended Impact: Designed to spark curiosity in school-age students by turning cold technical mission logs into heartwarming, memorable human-machine stories that honor NASA's engineering legacy.
